text:
sara: Heads up — nightly perf alerts show a surprising tail increase for torch.compile + cudagraphs when KV cache grows past ~512 tokens. Notable: same model, same commit, but +1.4x p99. Anyone seen cudagraph/graph-capture interacting with kernel autotuner like this?

aj: Can you paste the repro and a quick diff of the numbers?

sara: repro command I used:```
RW_ENABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 RW_AUTOTUNE=1 python -m bench.infer --model redwood/llama-13b --batch 1 --seqlens 128,1024 --warmup 60
```

sara: quick log excerpt:```
[2026-03-15 03:12:11] kernel_selector: picked matmul_tile16_v2 for seqlen=128 (latency=38.2ms)
[2026-03-15 03:12:16] kernel_selector: picked matmul_tile32_v1 for seqlen=1024 (latency=94.7ms)
[2026-03-15 03:12:16] cudagraph: capture handshake used cached graph (shapes=128) but runtime used seqlen=1024 -> fallback path triggered
```

sara: The capture handshake looks like it locked in kernels optimized for short seqlens, then when KV cache extended it didn't re-autotune and we saw a fallback that uses a slower kernel.

kevin: Interesting — that fallback path is the one that triggers extra workspace allocs and forces a different matmul kernel. Could be autotuner not being fed the longer sequence shapes during the warmup capture.

aj: Do we know whether torch.compile is preventing later kernel replacements? Maybe compilers/cudagraphs freeze the kernel map.

matt: I dug into the allocator traces, see this pprof snippet (trimmed):```
# p99 allocation spikes in cudagraph fallback
main::<lambda>  0.42s
matmul_tile32_v1  0.38s
matmul_tile16_v2  0.10s
```

matt: So the slower path is both choosing a different kernel and incurring extra allocation overhead.

jin: Quick mitigations: (1) expand warmup shapes in cudagraph capture to include representative long seqlens, or (2) disable cudagraphs when kv-cache growth is expected, or (3) make the autotuner probe tolerant to captures.

aj: For (3) we need a cheap probe that runs a short set of matmuls at larger seqlen before capture. Could be a toggle: AUTOTUNE_PROBE_BEFORE_CAPTURE=1.

kevin: Also saw a regression patch in last week's kernel scheduler PR that changed the match precedence for tile sizes. Might be a factor. I'll bisect.

ci-bot: CI check on branch perf-probe failed: 1 test unstable (bench/infer/p99 > baseline). See: https://ci.internal/1234

jin: I'll add a unit bench that captures multiple seqlens during warmup and a test that asserts kernel consistency post-capture. Quick PR after morning.

aj: Can someone file an incident/triage ticket with numbers? Put the p99 delta, repro, and recommended immediate mitigation (disable cudagraph for seqlen>512) so we can rollback fast if needed.

sara: Filed: INT-2026-0334 with logs and the command. For now I flipped cudagraph capture off on nightly to stop alerts.

matt: Two actionable follow-ups: 1) add autotune probe before capture (aj + jin), 2) adjust fallback to trigger a lightweight re-autotune when shapes diverge >20% (kevin + sara).

aj: I'll start the probe PR, will include a tiny micro-benchmark and an env flag to opt-out.

jin: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pulls/6789 — contains repro harness and probe stub.

kevin: Bisection shows the scheduler change contributed ~15% of the regression; the cudagraph capture + limited warmup accounts for the remainder. Good to know it's multi-factor.

aj: Thanks all — let's keep the mitigation in place until probe/patch lands. If anyone hits this in production let me know and I'll escalate. :thumbsup:
